    62  #include <config.h>
    63
    64  #include "idn2.h" /* IDN2_OK, ... */
    65
    66  /* Re-definitions to avoid modifying code below too much. */
    67  #define punycode_uint uint32_t
    68  #define punycode_success IDN2_OK
    69  #define punycode_overflow IDN2_PUNYCODE_OVERFLOW
    70  #define punycode_big_output IDN2_PUNYCODE_BIG_OUTPUT
    71  #define punycode_bad_input IDN2_PUNYCODE_BAD_INPUT
    72  #define punycode_decode _idn2_punycode_decode
    73
    74  /**********************************************************/
    75  /* Implementation (would normally go in its own .c file): */
    76
    77  #include <string.h>
    78
    79  #include "punycode.h"
    80
    81  /*** Bootstring parameters for Punycode ***/
    82
    83  enum { base = 36, tmin = 1, tmax = 26, skew = 38, damp = 700,
    84         initial_bias = 72, initial_n = 0x80, delimiter = 0x2D };
    85
    86  /* basic(cp) tests whether cp is a basic code point: */
    87  #define basic(cp) ((cp >= 'a' && cp <= 'z') || (cp >= '0' && cp <='9') || (cp >= 'A' && cp <='Z') || cp == 0x2D)
    88
    89  /* delim(cp) tests whether cp is a delimiter: */
    90  #define delim(cp) ((cp) == delimiter)
    91
    92  /* decode_digit(cp) returns the numeric value of a basic code */
    93  /* point (for use in representing integers) in the range 0 to */
    94  /* base-1, or base if cp does not represent a value.          */
    95
    96  static unsigned decode_digit(int cp)
    97  {
    98    if (cp >= 'a' && cp <= 'z')
    99      return cp - 'a';
   100    if (cp >= '0' && cp <= '9')
   101      return cp - '0' + 26;
   102    if (cp >= 'A' && cp <= 'Z')
   103      return cp - 'A';
   104
   105    return 0;
   106  }
   107
   108  /*** Platform-specific constants ***/
   109
   110  /* maxint is the maximum value of a punycode_uint variable: */
   111  static const punycode_uint maxint = -1;
   112  /* Because maxint is unsigned, -1 becomes the maximum value. */
   113
   114  /*** Bias adaptation function ***/
   115
   116  static punycode_uint adapt(
   117    punycode_uint delta, punycode_uint numpoints, int firsttime ) _GL_ATTRIBUTE_CONST;
   118
   119  static punycode_uint adapt(
   120    punycode_uint delta, punycode_uint numpoints, int firsttime )
   121  {
   122    punycode_uint k;
   123
   124    delta = firsttime ? delta / damp : delta >> 1;
   125    /* delta >> 1 is a faster way of doing delta / 2 */
   126    delta += delta / numpoints;
   127
   128    for (k = 0;  delta > ((base - tmin) * tmax) / 2;  k += base) {
   129      delta /= base - tmin;
   130    }
   131
   132    return k + (base - tmin + 1) * delta / (delta + skew);
   133  }
   134
   135  /*** Main decode function ***/
   136
   137  int punycode_decode(
   138    size_t input_length,
   139    const char input[],
   140    size_t *output_length,
   141    punycode_uint output[])
   142  {
   143    punycode_uint n, out, i, max_out, bias, oldi, w, k, digit, t;
   144    size_t b, j, in;
   145
   146    /* Initialize the state: */
   147
   148    n = initial_n;
   149    out = i = 0;
   150    max_out = *output_length > maxint ? maxint
   151              : (punycode_uint) *output_length;
   152    bias = initial_bias;
   153
   154    /* Handle the basic code points:  Let b be the number of input code */
   155    /* points before the last delimiter, or 0 if there is none, then    */
   156    /* copy the first b code points to the output.                      */
   157
   158    for (b = j = 0;  j < input_length;  ++j)  if (delim(input[j])) b = j;
   159    if (b > max_out) return punycode_big_output;
   160
   161    for (j = 0;  j < b;  ++j) {
   162      if (!basic(input[j])) return punycode_bad_input;
   163      output[out++] = input[j];
   164    }
   165    for (j = b + (b > 0);  j < input_length;  ++j)
   166      if (!basic(input[j])) return punycode_bad_input;
   167
   168    /* Main decoding loop:  Start just after the last delimiter if any  */
   169    /* basic code points were copied; start at the beginning otherwise. */
   170
   171    for (in = b > 0 ? b + 1 : 0;  in < input_length;  ++out) {
   172
   173      /* in is the index of the next ASCII code point to be consumed, */
   174      /* and out is the number of code points in the output array.    */
   175
   176      /* Decode a generalized variable-length integer into delta,  */
   177      /* which gets added to i.  The overflow checking is easier   */
   178      /* if we increase i as we go, then subtract off its starting */
   179      /* value at the end to obtain delta.                         */
   180
   181      for (oldi = i, w = 1, k = base;  ;  k += base) {
   182        if (in >= input_length) return punycode_bad_input;
   183        digit = decode_digit(input[in++]);
   184        if (digit >= base) return punycode_bad_input;
   185        if (digit > (maxint - i) / w) return punycode_overflow;
   186        i += digit * w;
   187        t = k <= bias /* + tmin */ ? tmin :     /* +tmin not needed */
   188            k >= bias + tmax ? tmax : k - bias;
   189        if (digit < t) break;
   190        if (w > maxint / (base - t)) return punycode_overflow;
   191        w *= (base - t);
   192      }
   193
   194      bias = adapt(i - oldi, out + 1, oldi == 0);
   195
   196      /* i was supposed to wrap around from out+1 to 0,   */
   197      /* incrementing n each time, so we'll fix that now: */
   198
   199      if (i / (out + 1) > maxint - n) return punycode_overflow;
   200      n += i / (out + 1);
   201      if (n > 0x10FFFF || (n >= 0xD800 && n <= 0xDBFF)) return punycode_bad_input;
   202      i %= (out + 1);
   203
   204      /* Insert n at position i of the output: */
   205
   206      /* not needed for Punycode: */
   207      /* if (basic(n)) return punycode_bad_input; */
   208      if (out >= max_out) return punycode_big_output;
   209
   210      memmove(output + i + 1, output + i, (out - i) * sizeof *output);
   211      output[i++] = n;
   212    }
   213
   214    *output_length = (size_t) out;
   215    /* cannot overflow because out <= old value of *output_length */
   216    return punycode_success;
   217  }
